rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abū Dharr reports from the Prophet that after sunset the sun ascends through the heavens, prostrates below the Throne, and seeks leave to rise; some versions say it waits until clothed with light and permitted to rise.
rows.anchor: روي هذا المعنى عن أبي ذر عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من طرق الخاصة والعامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says that if the sun report is sound, it must be interpreted figuratively.
rows.anchor: والرواية إن صحت فهي مؤولة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Salām ibn al-Mustanīr transmits from Abū Jaʿfar that God created the sun before the moon and light before darkness.
rows.anchor: وفي روضة الكافي بإسناده عن سلام بن المستنير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال إن الله عز وجل خلق الشمس قبل القمر

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Ashʿath reports al-Riḍā's answer: Cancer ascendant; Saturn Libra, Jupiter Cancer, Mars Capricorn, Sun Aries, Venus Pisces, Mercury Virgo, and Moon Taurus place the Sun in tenth house, so day preceded night; he also cited 36:40.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع روى العياشي في تفسيره بالإسناد عن الأشعث بن حاتم قال كنت بخراسان حيث اجتمع الرضا

rows.speaker: الآلوسي
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī questions the Qur'anic inference, grants the astrological calculation some basis, says a meridian-starting cycle accords with it, and suspects the report is inauthentic because al-Riḍā would not argue that way.
rows.anchor: نقل الآلوسي في روح المعاني هذا الحديث ثم قال وفي الاستدلال بالآية بحث ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-Ālūsī confused the actual nature of night and day when assessing the verse's argument.
rows.anchor: وقد اختلط عليه الأمر في تحصيل حقيقة معنى الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is night only as the privative counterpart of day, so its existence is preceded by day; the verse denies night preceding day in this natural sense.
rows.anchor: فمطلق الليل بمعناه الذي هو به ليل مسبوق الوجود بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse states a natural rule that preserves the ordered alternation of day and night: each night is the absence of the day that follows it, so cannot precede it.
rows.anchor: وقد استفيد منه الحكم بانحفاظ الترتيب في تعاقب الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says al-Ālūsī's claim that astronomy supports the report works only if astrology's premises are accepted as true, not merely in some general sense.
rows.anchor: وقول المعترض " وأما بالحساب فله وجه في الجملة " لا يدري وجه قوله في الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the meridian argument: infinitely many meridian circles pass through the poles and another point, so no unique point makes the Sun's placement there day for Earth.
rows.anchor: وكذا قوله " ورآى المنجمون أن ابتداء الدورة دائرة نصف النهار وله موافقة لما ذكر " لا محصل له

words: اتَّقُوا۟ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Ḥalabī reports that al-Ṣādiq interpreted what is before people as their sins and what is behind them as their punishment.
rows.anchor: روى الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال معناه اتقوا ما بين أيديكم من الذنوب وما خلفكم من العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not teaching the Prophet poetry means he was not able to compose it; it does not mean he could compose it but abstained because God forbade him.
rows.anchor: نفي أن يكون علمه الشعر ولازمه أن يكون بحيث لا يحسن قول الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase wards off an inference of deficiency or incapacity: God raised and purified the Prophet beyond poetry's invented embellishments and musical meters, fitting his mission and the inimitable Quran.
rows.anchor: فالجملة في مقام دفع الدخل والمحصل أن عدم تعليمنا إياه الشعر ليس يوجب نقصا فيه ولا أنه تعجيز له

words: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌۭ وَقُرْءَانٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restrictive construction is قصر القلب: the Quran is not poetry; it is a reminder and a clear Quran.
rows.anchor: فالحصر المستفاد من قوله { إن هو إلا ذكر } الخ من قصر القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause may attach either to God's not teaching the Prophet poetry or to the statement that what he recites is only reminder and clear Quran; both readings yield the same meaning.
rows.anchor: تعليل متعلق بقوله { وما علمناه الشعر } والمعنى ولم نعلمه الشعر لينذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being alive is a metaphor for understanding the truth and hearing it.
rows.anchor: وهو كناية عن كونه يعقل الحق ويسمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's purpose of warning the receptive and establishing the word against disbelievers echoes the opening of Sūrat Yā Sīn.
rows.anchor: فمحاذاة الآية لما في صدر السورة من الآيات في هذا المعنى ظاهر

words: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَا لَهُم مِّمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينَآ أَنْعَٰمًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock is a sign of God's oneness, lordship, and governance of human life, like the earlier signs of reviving earth, producing crops, and bringing forth springs.
rows.anchor: ذكر آية من آيات التوحيد تدل على ربوبيته تعالى وتدبيره للعالم الإنساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the livestock God's handiwork is a metaphor for His exclusive creation of them, with no participation by others.
rows.anchor: والمراد بكون الأنعام مما عملته أيديه تعالى عدم إشراكهم في خلقها واختصاصه به تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the livestock were created for humans, they are set apart for human use and ownership; conventional social ownership derives from this wider exclusivity.
rows.anchor: فإن الملك الاعتباري الذي في المجتمع من شعب الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possibility that Jonah's glorification meant praise before the fish swallowed him is weak and should not be adopted.
rows.anchor: فاحتمال كون المراد تسبيحه قبل التقام الحوت مرجوح لا ينبغي أن يصار إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah's glorification declared God free of what his departure from his people and going away seemed to imply.
rows.anchor: تسبيح له تعالى عما كان يشعر به فعله من ترك قومه وذهابه على وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of three views, the author prefers that Jonah glorified God specifically inside the fish; this glorification was the cause of his rescue from distress.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر أن المراد بتسبيحه نداؤه في الظلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His call in the darkness begins by affirming that only God is truly worshipped, then declares Him free of the implication that Jonah had turned away toward another.
rows.anchor: وقد قدم التهليل ليكون كالعلة المبينة لتسبيحه كأنه يقول لا معبود بالحق يتوجه إليه غيرك

words: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remaining in the fish until resurrection means remaining there perpetually until raised and brought out, like a person remaining in the grave; the author links this to 20:55.
rows.anchor: تأبيد مكثه في بطنه إلى أن يبعث فيخرج منه كالقبر الذي يقبر فيه الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not establish whether Jonah would remain alive or dead, whether the fish's body remained intact, which trumpet blast is meant, or whether resurrection idiomatically signals a long time.
rows.anchor: ولا دلالة في الآية على كونه عليه السلام على تقدير اللبث حيا في بطن الحوت إلى يوم يبعثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdh means casting or throwing away; al-ʿarāʾ is an exposed place with no roof, tent, or tree for shade. God cast Jonah out of the water there while he was ill.
rows.anchor: والعراء المكان الذي لا سترة فيه يستظل بها من سقف أو خباء أو شجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqṭīn is a kind of gourd with broad, rounded leaves; God grew it over Jonah to shade him.
rows.anchor: اليقطين من نوع القرع ويكون ورقه عريضا مستديرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here aw marks escalation and means بل; the people were the inhabitants of Nineveh.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهذه الجماعة أهل نينوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people believed in and followed Jonah, so God did not destroy them for the impending punishment and let them live until their appointed term.
rows.anchor: أي آمنوا به فلم نعذبهم ولم نهلكهم بما أشرف عليهم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context implies God sent Jonah back to the people a second time, and that their faith and following him came after their earlier belief and repentance when they saw the punishment.
rows.anchor: يدل على كون إرساله بأمر ثان وأن إيمانهم كان إيمانا ثانيا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some infer that Jonah's first mission to Nineveh preceded the fish, that he fled because he found the duty too difficult, and that God recommissioned him only after he was cast ashore; the author rejects this account.
rows.anchor: ما استدل بعضهم بالآيتين أن إرساله إلى القوم كان بعد خروجه من بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says 21:87 and 68:48 do not fit that account, and 10:98's language of removing punishment applies only to punishment already present or impending.
rows.anchor: إذ لا يطلق الكشف إلا في عذاب واقع حال أو مشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran recounts only parts of Jonah's and his people's story in al-Ṣāffāt: his mission, departure, ship, fish, rescue, renewed mission, and their belief.
rows.anchor: لم يتعرض القرآن الكريم إلا لطرف من قصته وقصة قومه فقد تعرض في سورة الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people rejected Jonah until the threatened punishment approached; seeing it, they all believed and repented, so God removed the punishment from them.
rows.anchor: فلما أشرف عليهم العذاب وشاهدوه مشاهدة عيان أجمعوا على الإيمان والتوبة إلى الله سبحانه فكشف الله عنهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah learned the punishment had lifted, apparently unaware of their belief and repentance; angry and displeased, he did not return and went away, appearing to flee his Lord and think God could not constrain him.
rows.anchor: وكأنه لم يعلم بإيمانهم وتوبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah boarded a laden ship; to save it, the crew cast lots for someone to throw to a great fish, Jonah was selected and cast into the sea, and the fish swallowed him as the ship escaped.
rows.anchor: فساهموا وقارعوا فيما بينهم فأصابت يونس عليه السلام فألقوه في البحر فابتلعه الحوت ونجت السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserved Jonah alive and well in the fish for days and nights; Jonah understood it as a trial for his action and called out in the fish's belly.
rows.anchor: حفظه حيا سويا في بطنه أياما وليالي ويونس عليه السلام يعلم أنها بلية ابتلاه الله بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Jonah, ordered the fish to cast him ashore sick, and grew a gourd tree over him for shade.
rows.anchor: فاستجاب الله له فأمر الحوت أن يلفظه فنبذه بالعراء وهو سقيم فأنبت الله سبحانه عليه شجرة من يقطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Jonah recovered, God sent him to the people again; they accepted his call and believed, and God let them enjoy life until their appointed term.
rows.anchor: ثم لما استقامت حاله أرسله إلى قومه فلبوا دعوته وآمنوا به فمتعهم الله إلى حين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Numerous reports from the Imams of the Prophet's household and some Sunni reports share the Quran's basic account of Jonah, while differing in incidental details.
rows.anchor: والأخبار الواردة من طرق أئمة أهل البيت عليه السلام على كثرتها وبعض الأخبار من طرق أهل السنة مشتركة المتون

rows.speaker: الآلوسي
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī's biblical account names Jonah as son of Amittai and says God ordered him to preach to huge Nineveh, which took about three days to cross; Jonah fled to Tarshish by way of Jaffa and boarded a ship.
rows.anchor: مذكور باسم يوناه بن إمتاي في مواضع من العهد القديم وكذا في مواضع من العهد الجديد

rows.speaker: الآلوسي
rows.claim: In al-Ālūsī's biblical account, frightened sailors throw cargo overboard; Jonah sleeps below, the captain wakes him to pray, and the crew cast lots to identify the cause of the storm.
rows.anchor: ففزع الملاحون ورموا في البحر بعض الأمتعة لتخف السفينة

rows.speaker: الآلوسي
rows.claim: The lot falls on Jonah; he identifies himself as servant of the Lord, maker of land and sea, and says to throw him overboard; the sailors try to reach shore, then cast him in and the sea calms.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم أنا عبد الرب إله السماء خالق البر والبحر وأخبرهم خبره

rows.speaker: الآلوسي
rows.claim: The biblical account says God sent a great fish that held Jonah three days and nights while he prayed; God released him on dry land and told him to go to Nineveh as commanded before.
rows.anchor: فبقي في بطنه ثلاثة أيام وثلاث ليال وصلى في بطنه إلى ربه واستغاث به

rows.speaker: الآلوسي
rows.claim: Jonah warned Nineveh it would be overthrown in three days; its people fasted and wore sackcloth, and the king ordered people and animals to abstain from food and drink and turn from evil, so God spared them.
rows.anchor: ونادى وقال يخسف نينوى بعد ثلاثة أيام فآمنت رجال نينوى بالله ونادوا بالصيام

rows.speaker: الآلوسي
rows.claim: In this account Jonah grieves that God showed mercy, asks to die, then grieves the lost gourd; God compares his pity for a plant he did not grow with God's care for over 120,000 uninformed people and many animals.
rows.anchor: فأنا لا أشفق على نينوى المدينة العظيمة التي فيها أكثر من اثنا عشر ربوة من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this account conflicts with the Quran by making Jonah flee his prophetic commission and resent the spared people despite knowing of their faith and repentance.
rows.anchor: وجهات اختلاف القصة مع ما يستفاد من القرآن الكريم ظاهرة كالفرار من الرسالة

words: مُغَاضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the biblical scriptures, which allow attributing even major sins to prophets, the Quran exempts prophets from sin, even minor sin; apparent implications must therefore be interpreted accordingly.
rows.anchor: بخلاف القرآن الكريم فإنه ينزه ساحتهم عن لوث المعاصي حتى الصغائر

words: مُغَاضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accordingly, the Quran's descriptions of Jonah as absconding, angry, and supposing God could not constrain him depict the apparent state and implication of his action, not actual sin.
rows.anchor: ولذا حملنا قوله { إذ أبق } وقوله { مغاضبا فظن أن لن نقدر } على حكاية الحال وإيهام فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God praises Jonah among the believers, says He chose him and made him righteous, and counts him among the prophets favored and guided to a straight path; divine election means choosing a servant exclusively for Himself.
rows.anchor: أثنى الله سبحانه عليه بأنه من المؤمنين وأنه اجتباه وقد عرفت أن اجتباءه إخلاصه العبد لنفسه خاصة

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says that when people cast lots while entrusting their affair to God, the true lot emerges; no judgment is fairer than a God-entrusted lot.
rows.anchor: وقال الصادق عليه السلام ما تقارع قوم ففوضوا أمرهم إلى الله عز وجل إلا خرج سهم الحق

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: Ḥabba al-ʿUranī reports that ʿAlī said God presented his wilayah to heaven and earth; Jonah rejected it, so God held him in the fish until he affirmed it. The author notes similar reports.
rows.anchor: عن حبة العرني قال قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام إن الله عرض ولايتي على أهل السماوات وعلى أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Universal divine wilayah means God takes charge of the servant, who turns only to Him and wills only what He wills through servitude that ends in God's exclusive election of him.
rows.anchor: والمراد الولاية الكلية الإلهية التي هو عليه السلام أول من فتح بابها من هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah's conduct displeased God and could not be ascribed to God's will; the trial made him acknowledge his own wrong and God's purity from willing such an act.
rows.anchor: فابتلاه الله بما ابتلاه ليعترف بظلمه على نفسه وأنه تعالى منزه عن إرادة مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trials of God's intimate servants are divine training that completes them and raises their rank, though some also include reproach; a proverb says trial accompanies intimacy.
rows.anchor: فالبلايا والمحن التي يبتلى بها الأولياء من التربية الإلهية التي يربيهم بها ويكملهم ويرفع درجاتهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū Baṣīr reports that al-Ṣādiq explained God diverted Nineveh's punishment because He knew they would repent, but concealed this from Jonah to devote him to worship in the fish and earn reward and honor.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام لأي علة صرف الله العذاب عن قوم يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding Judgment scene is linked to verses saying kinship will be gone, no soul can aid another, and the believer returns to family happily.
rows.anchor: يوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulal is the plural of ẓullah, a high covering; the fire's shades above and below the people enclose them.
rows.anchor: الظلل جمع ظلة وهي - كما قيل - الستر العالي

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines ṭāghūt as every transgressor and every object worshipped apart from God, and says the term is used for singular and plural.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الطاغوت عبارة عن كل متعد وكل معبود من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse most likely means idols and every false deity worshipped apart from God.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بها في الآية الأوثان وكل معبود طاغ من دون الله

words: ٱجْتَنَبُوا۟ ٱلطَّٰغُوتَ أَن يَعْبُدُوهَا وَأَنَابُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding false worship alone is insufficient; what benefits people is both negation and affirmation: worshipping God alone and sincerely leaving every other object of worship.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن مجرد النفي لا يجدي شيئا بل الذي ينفع الإنسان مجموع النفي والإثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase announces glad tidings and serves as the predicate about those who avoid the false deities and turn to God.
rows.anchor: قوله { لهم البشرى } إنشاء بشرى وخبر لقوله { والذين اجتنبوا } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording could have said give them glad tidings; calling them My servants honors them, then characterizes them as people who listen to speech and follow its best.
rows.anchor: فبشر عباد واضيف إلى ضمير التكلم لتشريفهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the following phrase about acting on speech, al-qawl means speech with some connection to action; its best form gives the surest guidance to truth and sincere counsel.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقول بقرينة ما ذكر من الإتباع ماله نوع ارتباط ومساس بالعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People drawn to beauty move from good to better when they encounter it; choosing only the good when a better option exists shows they were not responding to goodness itself.
rows.anchor: والإنسان إذا كان ممن يحب الحسن وينجذب إلى الجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the best means pursuing truth and guidance: choose truth over falsehood and the more rightly guided course over the less guided one.
rows.anchor: فكلما دار الأمر بين الحق والباطل والرشد والغي اتبعوا الحق والرشد وتركوا الباطل والغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They listen hoping to find truth and fearing they may miss it; they do not dismiss speech on first hearing to follow their own desires without reflection and understanding.
rows.anchor: ولا يردون قولا بمجرد ما قرع سمعهم اتباعا لهوى أنفسهم من غير أن يتدبروا فيه ويفقهوه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view limits the phrase to hearing the Quran and other speech, then following the Quran; the author rejects this as an unsupported restriction.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد باستماع القول واتباع أحسنه استماع القرآن وغيره واتباع القرآن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view restricts it to choosing the best divine commands, such as pardon over retribution or private over public almsgiving; the author likewise calls this unsupported specification.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد استماع أوامر الله تعالى واتباع أحسنها كالقصاص والعفو فيتبعون العفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This trait is God's general guidance: seeking truth and being ready to follow it wherever found, the basis to which all detailed guidance to divine truths leads.
rows.anchor: هذه الصفة هي الهداية الإلهية وهذه الهداية أعني طلب الحق والتهيؤ التام لاتباع الحق أينما وجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with sound intellects are guided to truth; their sign is following truth.
rows.anchor: ويستفاد منه أن العقل هو الذي به الاهتداء إلى الحق وآيته صفة اتباع الحق
